record.paper_title: Multiplier sequences, classes of generalized Bessel functions and open problems
record.original_question: Let p(x)=sum_{j=0}^n a_j x^j be a real polynomial with a_j>=0 for every j. A sequence {gamma_k}_{k>=0} is a classical multiplier sequence if T[x^k]=gamma_k x^k preserves real-rootedness of real polynomials. A sequence is a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS) if the same diagonal operator never increases the number of nonreal zeros of any real polynomial, counted with multiplicity. Find necessary and sufficient conditions on p(x) such that {p(k)/k!}_{k>=0} is a classical multiplier sequence, and find necessary and sufficient conditions on p(x) such that {p(k)/k!}_{k>=0} is a CZDS.

evidence.quote: Problem 36. Let p(x) := sum_{k=0}^n a_k x^k, where a_k >= 0 (k >= 0). Find conditions on p(x) such that (a) {p(k)/k!}_0^infinity is a multiplier sequence and (b) {p(k)/k!}_0^infinity is a CZDS.

Definition 4. A sequence of real numbers {gamma_k}_0^infinity is called a complex zero decreasing sequence, or CZDS, if the linear operator T defined by T[x^k]=gamma_k x^k has the property that for every real polynomial p(x), Z_C(T[p(x)]) <= Z_C(p(x)).

Definition 5. A sequence of real numbers {gamma_k}_0^infinity is called a classical multiplier sequence if the associated linear operator T defined by T[x^k]=gamma_k x^k has the property that for every real polynomial p(x), Z_C(T[p(x)])=0 whenever Z_C(p(x))=0.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. For a real polynomial f(x), let Z_C(f) denote the number of nonreal zeros of f, counted with multiplicity. Given a sequence of real numbers {γ_k}_{k≥0}, let T be the linear operator defined on the basis of monomials by T[x^k] = γ_k x^k and extended linearly to all real polynomials.

(i) The sequence {γ_k}_{k≥0} is called a classical multiplier sequence if for every real polynomial f(x) one has: Z_C(f) = 0 implies Z_C(T[f]) = 0 (equivalently, T preserves the set of real polynomials all of whose zeros are real).

(ii) The sequence {γ_k}_{k≥0} is called a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS) if for every real polynomial f(x) one has Z_C(T[f]) ≤ Z_C(f).

Problem. Let n ≥ 0 be an integer and let
   p(x) = a_0 + a_1 x + a_2 x^2 + ⋯ + a_n x^n
be a real polynomial with nonnegative coefficients, i.e. a_j ≥ 0 for every j ∈ {0,1,…,n}. Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the coefficients (a_0, a_1, …, a_n) (equivalently, on the polynomial p) so that:

(a) the sequence { p(k)/k! }_{k≥0} is a classical multiplier sequence;

(b) the sequence { p(k)/k! }_{k≥0} is a complex zero decreasing sequence (CZDS).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of characterizing those nonnegative-coefficient polynomials p(x) for which {p(k)/k!} is a multiplier sequence or a CZDS is a long-standing open question in the theory of multiplier sequences (Craven–Csordas program). Partial results exist (e.g., Laguerre's theorem giving sufficient conditions when p has only negative real zeros, and results on quadratic/cubic p), but no necessary-and-sufficient characterization is known. Recent papers in the area continue to treat this as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Complex Zero Decreasing Sequences — Craven and Csordas
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on CZDS lists characterization of polynomially-generated CZDS as an open problem; only partial sufficient conditions are known.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of fully characterizing polynomials p with {p(k)/k!} a CZDS or multiplier sequence remains open.

status_evidence.title: Multiplier sequences and Laguerre-Pólya class (arXiv:1505.00355)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses connection between sequences γ_k/k! and entire functions in the Laguerre–Pólya class, providing partial results but not a complete characterization for p(k)/k!.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial (sufficient) conditions of Laguerre type are established.
